title: Rounding All the Way & Word Problems

discoveryHook.scenario: The average cost to raise a child to age 18 is about $310,000. Rounded 'all the way', it becomes $300,000 — quick, easy, and still useful for planning. Rounding all the way means rounding to the first digit, leaving only one nonzero digit.

deepThink.prompt: What does 'rounding all the way' mean? Why would you ever want to round a number to only one nonzero digit?

explanation: Rounding all the way is simply rounding to the leftmost digit. After rounding, only that digit remains nonzero; all others become zeros.
Use the same rounding steps: identify the leftmost digit, look at the digit to its right, round up if ≥5, then change all other digits to zeros.
[[imp:This method gives the roughest approximation, but it's great for quick estimates and checking reasonableness of answers.]]
In word problems, use the Blueprint Aid: list Facts, what you're Solving for, Steps to take, and Key Points. Then convert verbal numbers to numeric before rounding.

formulaCard.title: Rounding all the way
formulaCard.formula: Keep only the first digit nonzero; all others zero.
notes: 2. If the next digit ≥5, add 1 to the leftmost digit.
3. Change all other digits to zeros.

examples.title: Example A — simple rounding all the way
steps: Leftmost digit is 7. Next digit is 8 (≥5) → round 7 up to 8.

examples.title: Example B — millions
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to a partner why the first digit 1 becomes 2.
steps: Leftmost digit is 1 (hundred‑millions). Next digit is 9 (≥5) → 1 becomes 2.
Change all other digits to zeros: $200,000,000.

examples.title: Example C — profit word problem
examples.prompt: Tootsie Roll's profit was twenty‑two million, five hundred fifty‑six thousand dollars. Round this profit all the way.
steps: Leftmost digit is 2 (ten‑millions). Next digit is 2 (<5) → keep 2.

brainDump.prompt: Without looking: explain 'round all the way' and round $5,181,000 all the way.

confusionCorner.title: Watch out!
confusionCorner.body: [[imp:Students sometimes round each digit individually — that's wrong. Only one digit remains nonzero.]] Also, always convert verbal numbers to numeric before rounding.

hints: Leftmost digit is 6; look at the next digit to decide whether to round up.
Replace every digit after the thousands place with zeros.
Leftmost digit is 4; the next digit is 7 (≥5).
After you adjust the thousands digit, zero out all places to the right.

questions.prompt: Kellogg's sales were five million, one hundred eighty‑one thousand dollars. Round this sales figure all the way.
hints: Convert to numeric first: $5,181,000. Find the leftmost digit and the digit to its right.
The next digit is less than 5, so the leftmost digit stays the same — then zero out the rest.

challengeCorner.prompt: A company's profit was $502,000. Round this profit all the way.
hints: Leftmost digit is 5; look at the hundred-thousands digit next.
That next digit is less than 5, so keep the 5 and change the remaining places to zeros.

presenterNotes: Demonstrate the Blueprint Aid on the board for the Tootsie Roll example.
Stress that rounding all the way gives a rough but fast approximation.
teacherCues: <!-- TEACHER CUE: Ask: 'Why would a manager want numbers rounded all the way?' -->
<!-- TEACHER CUE: After word problem, ask: 'Did anyone get a different rounded number? Why?' -->
